summary: Reproduced that SchedulerKvEventsPublisher emitted max_total_num_tokens directly as kv_total_blocks and scaled the same token capacity for kv_active_blocks. The scheduler now passes page_size to the publisher, which reports both fields using max_total_num_tokens // page_size. Added a regression for the reported page_size=16 example plus page_size=1, empty-cache, and partial-trailing-page boundaries.

tests.what_was_measured: On the base implementation, max_total_num_tokens=8192 and token_usage=0.5 emitted kv_total_blocks=8192 and kv_active_blocks=4096; the page_size=16 references are 512 and 256.

The added regression failed before the fix because SchedulerKvEventsPublisher had no page_size input; all four page-unit cases failed. Raw output is in reports/j-0fdd5b6f6a37/raw/regression-before.log.

One test and four subtests passed: page_size=16 at 50% usage, page_size=1 compatibility, zero active usage, and floor division for a partial trailing page. Raw output is in reports/j-0fdd5b6f6a37/raw/regression-after.log.
Adjacent scheduler-component and KV-event tests passed: 16 tests and 22 subtests. Raw output is in reports/j-0fdd5b6f6a37/raw/related-tests.log.
The complete change has no whitespace errors.

gpu_execution.evidence: The defect and correction are CPU-side scheduler metric accounting and mocked socket serialization; no model, tensor, kernel, or GPU execution path is involved. No unrelated GPU smoke was used as evidence.

remaining_limitations: No full serving/model run was performed because this unit conversion does not depend on weights or engine GPU execution.
The prepared interpreter does not include the ruff module; formatting was reviewed through the focused diff and git diff --check instead.
Two related upstream pull requests, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32499 and https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32558, remain open; this task did not modify or notify upstream.
